meta.source: RUN = Wietse Venema, Building Serverless Applications with Google Cloud Run (O'Reilly, 1st edition, Dec/2020; 204 pages in the PDF)
meta.page_convention: PDF page = printed page + 28 (chapters 1-10 = PDF 29-188). Back-of-book index = PDF 189-204 (not a source).
meta.labels: rules = stated in the book (with page); not_in_book = NOT in the book: may only be said as [inference], [extrapolation] or [DATED]. Every 2020 number/flag/price is [DATED].

serverless_definicao.name: What serverless is (according to the author)
serverless_definicao.summary: Serverless = simple DX without managing infrastructure, scale out of the box and pay-per-use; not to be confused with FaaS.
rules: Three ideas: no infrastructure, scale out of the box, pay-per-use (RUN p.30)
Still up to you: secure code, resources, scaling limits, access policies (RUN p.31)
Billing with 100 ms granularity + a fee per million requests (RUN p.32) [DATED]
Can cost more if utilization is already ~100%; 20-40% is common (RUN p.32)
Cloud Run is serverless and goes beyond FaaS (RUN p.33)
not_in_book: current prices, per-instance billing and allocated CPU [DATED]

preocupacoes_serverless.name: Concerns about serverless
preocupacoes_serverless.summary: Unpredictable costs, hyper-scalability against downstream systems, vendor dependency and latency from compute/storage separation.
rules: Cost is a quality attribute; limit scale and run load tests (RUN p.39)
Relational databases and rate-limited APIs suffer from fast scaling (RUN p.39)
Portability: container + Knative compatibility (RUN p.40)
not_in_book: billing budgets and alerts beyond a mention (RUN p.42)

produtos_gcp_serverless.name: GCP serverless products (Table 1-1) and choosing Run/Functions/App Engine
produtos_gcp_serverless.summary: Cloud Functions = glue, App Engine = source-based PaaS, Cloud Run = request-oriented containers; Table 1-1 lists OSS compatibility.
rules: Functions: one endpoint, one container per request, no traffic splitting (RUN p.58)
App Engine Flexible runs on Compute Engine; Standard on the same platform as Run/Functions (RUN p.58)
Differences: source vs container, request vs instance (RUN p.59)
The future of App Engine/Functions is the author's speculation (RUN p.59-60)
not_in_book: Cloud Run functions, Jobs and products after 2020 [DATED]

service_revision_trafego.name: Service, revision, rollback and tags
service_revision_trafego.summary: A service has an endpoint; each change creates an immutable revision; traffic can go 100% to the latest, be gradual or tested on a separate URL; rollback via update-traffic.
rules: Revision = immutable copy of the config (image, env, serving, resources, scaling, identity) (RUN p.48)
Default: 100% of traffic on the latest revision (RUN p.48)
Rollback: gcloud run services update-traffic NAME --to-revisions REV=100 (RUN p.49)
Old revisions disappear automatically above a thousand (RUN p.49) [DATED]
Tags: concept only, no command (RUN p.49)

ciclo_de_vida_container.name: Container life cycle (SIGTERM, shutdown)
ciclo_de_vida_container.summary: Image cached; receives requests once it listens on 8080; CPU throttled on scale down; shutdown with SIGTERM and a short grace period (~10 s).
rules: You do not choose which containers die (RUN p.50)
SIGTERM: close connections and flush buffers; ~10 s (RUN p.50) [DATED]

cpu_throttling_background.name: CPU throttling and background work
cpu_throttling_background.summary: Outside requests the CPU is nearly zero; background work may never finish; use Cloud Tasks.
rules: Full CPU only while serving a request (RUN p.52)
Background work after the response is not reliable; heavy work causes 503 at startup (RUN p.52)
Reliable alternative: Cloud Tasks + worker (RUN p.127-129)

concorrencia_autoscaling.name: Concurrency, request buffer and autoscaler
concorrencia_autoscaling.summary: Slots per container; the autoscaler acts on free slots and CPU; default ceiling of a thousand containers with 429 at the limit; default concurrency 250 (2020) tends to be high.
rules: --concurrency 1 for CPU-intensive or non-thread-safe apps (RUN p.54)
Default ceiling 1000; at the limit, HTTP 429; more requires a quota (RUN p.54) [DATED]
Default concurrency 250 in Nov/2020, probably high (RUN p.55) [DATED]
Tune concurrency so the autoscaler reacts to slots, not CPU (RUN p.55)
not_in_book: current autoscaling algorithm, CPU utilization targets

cold_start.name: Cold start and minimum instances
cold_start.summary: A request waits in the buffer until the container opens 8080; conceptual mitigation: minimum instances; pool of throttled containers.
rules: Happens after a new deploy or a period without traffic; less likely on scale up (RUN p.55)
Minimum instances keep containers ready (RUN p.55)
Ready in seconds shortens deploy time (RUN p.38)
not_in_book: runtime optimizations per language beyond Go/GraalVM (RUN p.77)

disco_memoria_prontidao.name: In-memory disk, readiness and 5xx
disco_memoria_prontidao.summary: Containers are disposable; filesystem in memory (4 GB in 2020); readiness = accepting a connection on 8080; more than 20 consecutive 5xx remove the container.
rules: What you can keep: rebuildable cache, per-request temp, templates, connections (RUN p.55-56)
Filesystem in memory, 4 GB limit in Oct/2020 (RUN p.56) [DATED]
There is no way to change the readiness check (RUN p.56)
More than 20 consecutive 5xx responses -> container replaced (RUN p.56) [DATED]

containers_dockerfile.name: Containers and Dockerfile (introduction)
containers_dockerfile.summary: Introduction to containers, Dockerfile instructions, small images with multi-stage and distroless.
rules: Instructions FROM, COPY, RUN, WORKDIR, ENV, ENTRYPOINT; prefer COPY/ENTRYPOINT (RUN p.69-70)
826 MB (golang) vs 26.7 MB (distroless multi-stage) (RUN p.71-72)
Snyk 2019: base images with 30+ vulnerable libs (RUN p.71)
not_in_book: advanced Docker/Kubernetes: hand off to containers-docker-kubernetes-expert

build_sem_dockerfile.name: ko, Jib and Buildpacks
build_sem_dockerfile.summary: Three ways to build an image without a Dockerfile; ko uses service.yml with ko:// and replace.
rules: ko: KO_DOCKER_REPO; ko publish; ko resolve | gcloud beta run services replace - (RUN p.75-76)
Jib: mvn compile jib:dockerBuild; 627 MB vs 197 MB (RUN p.77)
pack build --builder gcr.io/buildpacks/builder:v1; Go, Node.js, Python, Java, .NET Core (RUN p.78) [DATED]
not_in_book: current buildpacks and languages supported today [DATED]

artifact_registry.name: Artifact Registry
artifact_registry.summary: Regional/multi-regional repository; URL us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/REPO/IMG; auth configure-docker.
rules: gcloud artifacts repositories create --location us --repository-format docker NAME (RUN p.73)
gcloud auth configure-docker us-docker.pkg.dev (RUN p.74)
Tension: the text says only AR is accepted (RUN p.72) but the 1st deploy uses gcr.io (RUN p.45) [DATED]

cloud_build.name: Cloud Build and CI
cloud_build.summary: Remote Docker build; cloudbuild.yaml with steps in containers; GitHub triggers; 24 h timeout.
rules: gcloud builds submit --tag IMG (RUN p.79)
Sequential steps in /workspace; a failure stops the build (RUN p.79-81)
Can deploy to Cloud Run and run migrations (24 h timeout) (RUN p.81) [DATED]
Triggers per commit; wizard in the console (RUN p.81-82)
not_in_book: Cloud Deploy, promotion between environments, Binary Authorization

cloud_sql.name: Cloud SQL with Cloud Run (Proxy, IP, security)
cloud_sql.summary: Use the managed Proxy (--add-cloudsql-instances, UNIX socket); avoid direct connection; harden users; same region.
rules: Proxy: TLS and IAM (Cloud SQL Client role) (RUN p.86-87)
--add-cloudsql-instances PROJ:REG:INST creates a socket at /cloudsql/ (RUN p.89-91)
Direct connection not recommended; --require-ssl (RUN p.90)
Delete root@% and create via cloudsqlproxy~%; in production a non-admin user (RUN p.88-89)
Not serverless; ~US$ 9/month in Sep/2020 (RUN p.86) [DATED]
not_in_book: Cloud SQL Auth Proxy v2, language connectors, IAM database auth

banco_concorrencia_pool.name: Limiting concurrency against the database (max-instances and pool)
banco_concorrencia_pool.summary: The database degrades above the optimum (a small multiple of vCPUs); control via --max-instances and connection pool; external pool if needed.
rules: Optimal concurrency: a small multiple of vCPUs; real case ~110 on 16 vCPU (RUN p.94, 97)
gcloud run services update todo --max-instances 100 (RUN p.96)
db.SetMaxOpenConns(2): active connections = max instances x 2 (RUN p.96)
External pool (PgBouncer on a VM) for PostgreSQL (RUN p.96)
not_in_book: managed Cloud SQL connection pooling, RDS Proxy-like
optimal max-instances value for your case: measure

cloud_sql_producao.name: Cloud SQL in production (HA, backups, resilience)
cloud_sql_producao.summary: Monitor CPU; storage increase; HA across two zones; app resilient to ~1 min of downtime; enable backups.
rules: HA = two instances in different zones (RUN p.97)
Even with HA, tolerate ~1 minute of unavailability (RUN p.98)
Enable automated backups (RUN p.98)
not_in_book: point-in-time recovery, read replicas, detailed scheduled maintenance

sessoes_memorystore.name: HTTP sessions and Memorystore
sessoes_memorystore.summary: Session in an external store (Redis/Memorystore, Firestore, Cloud SQL); signed cookie; session affinity not supported in 2020 and never meant for data.
rules: Cookie with ID and signature; Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict (RUN p.100-101)
Memorystore: basic/standard tier, private IP only, no size autoscaling (RUN p.101-102)
SLAs: Memorystore 99.9%, Cloud SQL HA 99.95%, Firestore multi ~26.3 s/month (RUN p.106) [DATED]
Session affinity not supported in Sep/2020; best-effort; do not store sessions in containers (RUN p.106-107) [DATED]

vpc_connector.name: VPC Connector and private IP
vpc_connector.summary: Cloud Run is outside the VPC; the Connector (16-IP range, 2-10 instances, billed while idle) carries traffic to private IPs.
rules: /28 range (16 IPs); traffic to a private IP goes through the Connector, public goes to the internet (RUN p.102-103)
Minimum 2 and maximum 10 instances; not pay-per-use (~US$ 8/month in Sep/2020) (RUN p.104) [DATED]
gcloud compute networks vpc-access connectors create ... --range 10.0.0.0/28; --vpc-connector (RUN p.104-105)
Delete when done (RUN p.108)

iam_roles_bindings.name: IAM: roles, policy bindings, allUsers
iam_roles_bindings.summary: Roles group permissions; a binding links a member to a role; Invoker can be per service; --allow-unauthenticated = allUsers binding.
rules: Least privilege (RUN p.109)
Cloud Run Invoker on a project or on a service (RUN p.112)
--allow-unauthenticated adds an allUsers+run.invoker binding (RUN p.112-113)
not_in_book: custom roles, IAM Conditions, Org Policy, VPC Service Controls

service_account.name: Service accounts of the service and the default account
service_account.summary: Every service has a service account; the default one has Project Editor and should not go to production; create one per service.
rules: Default = Project Editor (more than 3000 permissions) (RUN p.114)
gcloud iam service-accounts create + --service-account (RUN p.115)
One account per service and minimal bindings (RUN p.124-125)

id_token_autenticacao.name: ID token and private service
id_token_autenticacao.summary: A private service requires an ID token (Bearer); valid up to 1 h; audience = target service; idtoken library.
rules: gcloud auth print-identity-token; Authorization: Bearer (RUN p.117-118)
Criteria: Google signature, audience, not expired, Invoker binding (RUN p.118)
Invalid requests are not billed (RUN p.118)
idtoken.NewClient(ctx, audience) renews and is valid only for that target (RUN p.118)
not_in_book: end-user authentication (IAP, Identity Platform, Firebase Auth)

gfe_latencia.name: Google Frontend and latency between services
gfe_latencia.summary: Calls between services go through the GFE (+7-9 ms); prefer coarse-grained integration.
rules: GFE: TLS, DoS, checks authorization, strips reserved headers (RUN p.119)
Minimum extra latency of 7-9 ms (author's benchmark) (RUN p.120) [DATED]
Fine-grained sequential calls and naive parallelism cause problems (RUN p.120)

cloud_tasks.name: Cloud Tasks and worker
cloud_tasks.summary: Cloud Tasks schedules and runs HTTP requests to a Cloud Run worker with retry and rate limit; duplicate delivery is possible.
rules: Success = 2xx; deadline 10 min default, up to 30 (RUN p.129) [DATED]
ID token added at execution; the creator needs Service Account User (RUN p.132-133)
Retry: minBackoff, maxBackoff, maxDoublings, maxAttempts (RUN p.133-135)
Rate limit: maxDispatchesPerSecond, maxConcurrentDispatches; default 1000 is high (RUN p.134)
Duplicate delivery < 0.001%: record state in a database (RUN p.135)

terraform_iac.name: Infrastructure as code with Terraform
terraform_iac.summary: Declarative IaC; init/plan/apply; state contains secrets; ADC instead of a key; no gradual rollout.
rules: plan -out tfplan; apply tfplan; apply without a plan asks for 'yes' (RUN p.148-149, 153)
State may contain secrets (RUN p.150)
ADC, never a downloaded service account key (RUN p.143-144)
Terraform does not manage gradual rollout in Cloud Run (RUN p.143)
Dependencies via references (RUN p.153-154)

logs_estruturados.name: Structured logs and severity
logs_estruturados.summary: Cloud Run captures stdout/stderr, /var/log and syslog; JSON with severity becomes attributes; avoid client libraries and PII.
rules: Captures streams, /var/log and syslog + request log (RUN p.157-158)
Plain text = default severity; JSON with severity (RUN p.160-161)
Client libraries hurt portability (RUN p.162)
Level table DEBUG..ALERT (RUN p.163)
No PII in logs (RUN p.163, 173)

tracing_contexto.name: Request context and trace
tracing_contexto.summary: The GFE injects X-Cloud-Trace-Context; put the trace ID in the logs and propagate it in calls; log-based metrics for alerts.
rules: Attribute logging.googleapis.com/trace groups the logs of one request (RUN p.166)
Propagate trace via context with OpenCensus + idtoken (RUN p.168-169)
Log-based metrics in the Logs-based metrics tab (RUN p.171-172)

knative_portabilidade.name: Knative Serving and portability
knative_portabilidade.summary: Cloud Run is compatible with (not a managed) Knative Serving; same service.yml; migrating from Run to Knative is easier than the reverse.
rules: Cloud Run is not managed Knative: a compatible, separate and proprietary implementation (RUN p.176)
Same service.yml: kubectl apply vs gcloud beta run services replace (RUN p.185-186)
K8s -> Run is harder: CronJob, gVisor (no NFS), throttling (RUN p.187)
Services without an open alternative: IAM, Firestore, Tasks, Scheduler (RUN p.188)
not_in_book: Cloud Run for Anthos, current Knative

custos_free_tier.name: Costs, free tier and shutting down
custos_free_tier.summary: US$ 300 in credits in 2020; serverless services with a free tier; Cloud SQL, Memorystore and VPC Connector charge while idle.
rules: US$ 300 in credits; account suspended when exhausted (RUN p.42) [DATED]
Cloud SQL, Memorystore have no free tier (RUN p.42)
Each chapter has a 'Shutting Down' section (RUN p.42, 82, 98, 108)

yaml_replace.name: Knative service.yml and gcloud replace
yaml_replace.summary: services describe --format yaml exports; replace applies authoritatively, except IAM.
rules: apiVersion serving.knative.dev/v1; kind Service; spec.template.spec.containers.image (RUN p.76)
replace overwrites the whole config except the IAM bindings (RUN p.76)
The same YAML runs on Knative (RUN p.185-186)
not_in_book: scaling annotations (autoscaling.knative.dev/...) and Cloud Run annotations (run.googleapis.com/...) in detail

limites_numericos.name: Numeric limits cited (2020)
limites_numericos.summary: A thousand instances, concurrency 250, disk/memory 4 GB, SIGTERM ~10 s, 20 5xx, max timeout 60 min: all from 2020.
rules: Instances: 1000 (RUN p.37, 54)
Default concurrency: 250 (RUN p.55)
In-memory disk: up to 4 GB (RUN p.56)
Max request timeout: 60 min (RUN p.129)
not_in_book: current CPU/memory limits per instance, request/response size, number of revisions [DATED]
